commits.message:
Locally verify the withdrawn-input journey families over staged L1 events

Stage real deposit and withdrawal events on an isolated emulator deployment
of the frozen blueprint, using the same request builders the live journeys
publish with, then run an event-bearing retained block through the
unmodified installed selector bound to the real deployment identity. Both
polarities are asserted for withdrawnInput and withdrawnReferenceInput,
plus exact proof preparation that refuses the honest control, so the two
fixtures move from candidates into the registered history fixtures.

Sign withdrawal bodies over their Aiken serialisation

The SDK signed blake2b(domain || Lucid-encoded body), while the on-chain
rule withdrawal_signature_is_valid_v1 and the fault-proof detectors verify
over cbor.serialise(body), which renders definite asset maps. Every honest
withdrawal published through the SDK therefore carried a signature the
protocol reads as invalid and was detected as a withdrawal mistag. The
signing preimage now uses the Aiken serialisation, and the validation
dispute replay compares the committed withdrawal leaf in its canonical
committed encoding instead of the plain Lucid encoding, which refused every
withdrawal-bearing block.

Repair the hermetic user-event-origin fixture and use the workspace test Postgres port

The user-event-origin fixture stubs fetch and WebSocket itself, so its red
was never a missing Kupo: its stub returned a quoted ETag that the source
rejects as a malformed checkpoint header, and its socket close never
dispatched the close event, so the Ogmios session close timed out. Both now
match the local-historical-capture fixture. The public retained DA store
suite defaulted POSTGRES_PORT to 5432 while the workspace test server runs
on 5433.

Record the publication encoding in journaled field-carriage actions

Journal-only recovery re-derived every publication digest as a §8.5
nothing-but-bytes datum, but structured-data-preimage requirements publish
the structured Data itself and address it over the datum CBOR. Reconcile
therefore reported a conflict for those publications and the
withdrawal-mistag and structured-data-preimage lifecycles failed. The
publication action now records its encoding next to the digest, and
recovery validates the encoding before re-deriving the content address.

The catalogue retained-classification fixture with an accepted descriptor
and a rejected terminal is now proved as an invalid one-step transition
instead of throwing a malformed-payload error, so the test asserts the
buildable fault.

Dispatch the startup-prepared fault target once workflow recovery finishes

Startup classification prepares its target without dispatching so journal
recovery can resume existing executions first, but finalized blocks that
leave the state queue untouched never re-enter dispatch. A fault selected
at startup on a quiet chain therefore sat with an empty proof queue until
the next queue movement, which is what stalled the installed-journey
emulator test at proof construction. Schedule the prepared target as its
own startup stage right after recovery.
Docs: agent guides, forced-inclusion verdict plan and size-plan ledger

Node and DA committee: published deployment journal and retained listener

The published-workflow deployment helper journals into a fresh directory and
takes the chain clock from the emulator, so a frozen emulator time never
trips the initialization validity check. The DA committee public retained
listener and its libp2p runtime test follow the transport changes.

Devnet watcher journeys harness

Add the devnet watcher-journeys harness: fixture catalogue and readiness
reports, transaction, forced, source, script and history cases against a
retained real deposit, the transition-trace journey runner with its timing
plan and coverage ring, retained DA and native-chain capture checks, and the
preprod run scripts.

mintItemNonCanonical joins the raw-source cases: the operator accepts a
transaction whose mint field carries a zero-quantity item, and the full
installed catalogue selects the family.

Fault proofs: replay prerequisites, field carriage and journal handoffs

Route unresolved replay conditions through typed prerequisites that the
complete-replay union can discharge, thread the field-carriage prerequisite
port through the affected families, and carry the central-journal and
authenticated-workflow updates for the families touched this cycle.

Watcher: local historical capture, deposit trace and finality fixtures

Carry the native chain-sync sidecar changes, the Kupo resolve_hashes script
shape and unquoted ETag handling in the local Kupmios source, the Ogmios
session close that waits for the physical socket, and the proof supervisor
and decision-bridge work.

Test fixtures follow: the boundary socket stub emits its close event, the
user-event-origin fixture renders resolved scripts as Kupo objects, the
finality chronology test expects the height-refined confirmation boundary,
and the published deposit trace uses the configured provider.

Add the mintItemNonCanonical fraud-proof family

Register category 00000036 end to end: the four Aiken step validators and
their library modules, the SDK contract bindings and catalogue entry, the
fault-proofs family (scan, evidence, central journal, submit steps and
workflow), the node/DA-committee deployment identity for 55 installed
categories, and the regenerated DA contract deployment fixture.

Sibling replayers that decode field 5 now yield a representable_field_shape
prerequisite when the mint-item scanner owns the transaction, so the
complete-replay union discharges it with the direct finding instead of
failing on the malformed item.

Add the trusted-head authority child-process fixture the watcher journeys import

watcher-installed-journey.test.ts already imported
tests/support/trusted-head-process-fixture.js, but the fixture, its forked
entry module, and its own runtime test had not been committed, so a clean
checkout could not typecheck the watcher package. The fixture bundles the
current authority source with esbuild and forks it onto its own event loop,
the way the deployed sidecar runs.

Stop reading necessity artifacts from the scanner-confinement gate

The gate that confines `canonical_cbor_scan_v1` to its reviewed on-chain
consumers also parsed three Markdown necessity artifacts under
docs/exec-plans/evidence/necessity and failed whenever their pinned blueprint
identity drifted from the live build. Those documents are not test inputs:
the consumer set is now an explicit list in the test, and the on-chain
source scan, the complete-item staging checks, and the predicate negative
controls stay exactly as they were.

Restore the local full-pass entrypoint and make the test Postgres durable

The workspace typecheck was reproducibly red: midgard-node and
midgard-node-tools prefixed `tsc --noEmit` with builds of lucid-midgard and
midgard-sdk, and under `--workspace-concurrency=4` those two prebuild chains
raced on `tsup --clean` of the same midgard-core dist (ENOENT on unlink), which
aborted run-test-lanes-v1.mjs before any lane started. The prefix has been
dead since every package resolved its siblings from source through the
`midgard-source` export condition, so typecheck is now `tsc --noEmit` alone.

The prefix did have one live side effect: midgard-node's crash-probe child
processes and midgard-node-tools' `node --test` files run under plain node,
which resolves the workspace packages to `dist/`. That build now belongs to a
`pretest` in those two packages, which lane B runs serially, so there is a
single dist builder at a time and `pnpm test` works from a clean checkout.

scripts/start-test-postgres.sh starts the 127.0.0.1:5433 test server the node
suites need with the settings they assert (synchronous_commit=on server-wide,
no unix socket, 200 connections), initialising a persistent data directory on
first use and leaving any server already on the port untouched.
